extracted.intended_audience: researchers, foundation staff, policy makers, and minority advocacy organizations interested in philanthropic support for Hispanic populations
extracted.subtask_description: A research monograph and survey instrument to measure and describe how U.S. private foundations supported Hispanic needs and concerns (1977-78), including grant patterns, institutional policies/procedures, and methodological guidance for researching foundation grantmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage of total foundation monies benefiting Hispanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the proportion of total foundation grant dollars that directly benefited Hispanics (e.g., 'Only 1% of the foundation grant dollars studied directly benefited Hispanics in the United States in 1977 and 1978').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report as percent of total dollars studied; note potential overstatement because the Foundation Grants Index may over-represent larger or more responsive foundations. Compare to prior studies to assess trends (e.g., a 0.27% increase since earlier study).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration of giving among foundations (single-foundation dominance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how much of Hispanic-directed support is concentrated in a small number of foundations (e.g., 'One foundation alone, the Ford Foundation, provided over half (54%) of the support for Hispanic needs and concerns').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report dollars and percent attributable to top donors; show effect of excluding the largest donor on overall percentages (e.g., excluding Ford reduces support to 0.5% of other foundations' dollars).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number/proportion of foundations that give to Hispanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Count how many foundations (and what proportion of those studied) made any grants for domestic Hispanic needs and concerns (e.g., 'Less than one-fourth of the foundations studied (95 out of 400) made any grants for domestic Hispanic needs and concerns').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both count and percent of total foundations in sample; consider comparing across time periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensity of foundation support (number of grants per foundation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure how many grants each foundation gave to Hispanic causes (e.g., 'Of these foundations, two-thirds (68%) gave only one or two grants in 1977 and 1978, while one-third (32%) gave three or more grants').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify foundations by number-of-grants bands (1, 2, 3+); report frequency distribution and identify whether support is episodic or sustained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnicity of beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify grants by ethnic beneficiary category: Chicano (Mexican-American), Puerto Rican, General Hispanic (not specifically Chicano/Puerto Rican), and Mixed (benefits Hispanic groups and other minorities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit coding rules (see methodological assumptions); report dollar amounts and counts by ethnicity and compare to past periods (e.g., share to Chicanos/Puerto Ricans decreased).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hispanic control of recipient agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the extent to which grants to benefit Hispanics went to Hispanic-run or Hispanic-controlled organizations (e.g., '51% of the money benefiting Hispanics went to Hispanic-run organizations').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report percent of dollars and number of grants to Hispanic-controlled vs non-Hispanic-controlled agencies; compare to earlier studies to assess changes in sensitivity to minority control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic distribution of grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze the regional distribution of grant dollars for Hispanic needs and concerns and compare to the regional distribution of the Hispanic population (e.g., Northeast received 40% of Hispanic grant dollars while having 13% of Hispanic population).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group states into predefined regions (Northeast, North Central, Southwest, etc.); compute adjusted regional shares and compare to demographic share; highlight regions under- or over-served.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields of interest receiving Hispanic-directed grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize grants by field (education, civil rights/legal services, health, arts/humanities, social sciences, community organization/development, religion, research, etc.) and measure dollar distribution across fields (e.g., education 36%, legal advocacy 25%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report number of grants, total dollars and average grant by field; identify which fields receive large or small shares and whether giving favors 'traditional' low-risk areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top recipient organizations (most favored donees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify individual recipient agencies receiving the largest number of grants and/or highest dollar amounts for Hispanic needs (e.g., MALDEF obtained almost one-third of monies given to Hispanic-controlled agencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List top donees with counts and dollar amounts; report concentration among donees (e.g., top 20 recipients received X% of funds to Hispanic agencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type/profile of foundations responsive to Hispanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterize foundations that gave to Hispanics by size (assets), type (community, corporate, family, general purpose, special purpose), and other organizational characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report distributions (e.g., foundations with assets over $1 million are over-represented among responsive foundations; community foundations over-represented; corporate under-represented).

rubrics_metrics.name: Total dollar amount of grants awarded (foundation-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify foundations by total grant dollars awarded in a given calendar year (e.g., categories: Less than $60,000; $60,000-$299,999; $300,000-$999,999; $1,000,000-$4,999,999; $5,000,000 or above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as a predictor of likelihood to support Hispanics (larger foundations more likely to support Hispanics); report cross-tabulations with responsive behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average grant amount (foundation-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure a foundation's average grant size using categories (e.g., Less than $3,000; $3,000-$9,999; $10,000-$24,999; $25,000-$49,999; $50,000 or above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to analyze whether responsive foundations favor small one-shot awards vs larger multi-year commitments; compare average sizes across fields and recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence and size of full-time administrative staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a foundation has a full-time administrative staff and the approximate number employed (survey question: 'Does this Foundation have a full-time administrative staff? If yes, indicate number').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsive foundations reported high full-time staffing (92%); use staffing as a signal of organizational capacity to engage with minority applicants and provide technical assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation publications and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the foundation issues publications such as annual reports, biennial reports, multi-annual reports, or general brochures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High incidence of annual/biennial reports among responsive foundations (83%); use publication practices as proxy for transparency and outreach to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation mailing list practices and Hispanic mailing list
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the foundation maintains a mailing list, whether it has a specific Hispanic mailing list, and whether organizations can request to be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report percent with general mailing list, percent with special Hispanic lists (only 11% reported having special Hispanic mailing lists); openness to inclusion reflects accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to prospective applicants' letters of inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the foundation responds to letters of inquiry from prospective applicants (Yes/No/Don't know).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 97% of responsive foundations claim to answer general information inquiries; report response rates for increasingly complex inquiries (deadlines/format/board dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information provided to applicants on request
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether foundations provide specific application information: application deadlines; suggestions for proposal contents (length/format); dates of Executive Board meetings; feedback on preliminary drafts/concept papers; advice on other funding sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report availability percentages per item (e.g., fewer foundations respond to complex queries about format/deadlines). Use as measure of applicant support and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of proposal receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether foundations send a written acknowledgement upon receipt of proposals (survey: 'Upon receipt of proposals, does the Foundation respond with a written acknowledgement?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 88% of responsive foundations claimed to send written acknowledgements; consider as basic courtesy and procedural transparency metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notification to unsuccessful applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the foundation communicates its decision in writing to unsuccessful applicants (Yes/No/Don't know).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 95% of responsive foundations report sending written rejection notices; use as measure of accountability and communication practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation to unsuccessful applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and to what extent the foundation explains the reasons for proposal rejection (survey: 'Will the Foundation explain to unsuccessful applicants the reason for their lack of success?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record yes/no/NA; identify whether unsuccessful applicants are given substantive feedback or only notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice on alternate funding sources to unsuccessful applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the foundation advises unsuccessful applicants on alternative sources of funding for their projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 44% reported offering advice on other funding sources, but less often to unsuccessful applicants; use as metric of supportive follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation actions for worthy but poorly drafted proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Likely actions foundations take when a proposal is conceptually strong but poorly written (options include: no approval; encourage revision and resubmission; no further advice; contact for additional information; offer technical assistance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey records which actions are probable; presence of technical assistance or revision encouragement indicates applicant-friendly practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of technical assistance / staff for applicant assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the foundation has staff who provide technical assistance to applicants (Yes/No/Don't know) and the extent of feedback on drafts/concept papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 64% reported feedback on drafts, but only 25% claimed staff expressly to provide technical assistance; this distinction affects minority applicants' capacity to submit fundable proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundations' suggested improvements for minority applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundations were asked to suggest five ways minority groups could improve their funding prospects (open-ended suggestions captured: study guidelines, conduct research to target foundations, improve proposal contents/structure, strengthen management/budgeting/fundraising).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize frequency of suggested actions; use to create best-practice guidance for applicant organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for educational research & development activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the foundation supports specific educational R&D activities: internships, graduate fellowships, postdocs, conferences, surveys, community educational needs assessments, ongoing research by organizations or individuals, publication of results, seminars/workshops, other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report which activities are currently supported and were supported over past five years; cross-tabulate with Hispanic-conducted R&D support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for educational R&D conducted by Hispanics (past 5 years and current)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether foundations have supported educational R&D conducted by Hispanics over the past five years and whether they currently support such activities (with activity-type breakdown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture program types supported (internships, fellowships, conferences, etc.) and distribution by foundation size; use to assess targeted capacity-building support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of persons of Hispanic origin on boards/trustees
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there are persons of Hispanic origin serving on the foundation's Board of Directors or Trustees and counts by subgroup (Mexican American, Puerto Rican, Cuban, Latin American).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record counts by subgroup; compare incidence to national baselines (noting Council on Foundations estimate of 0.3% of all foundations having minority Board members). Use as indicator of governance diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment of Hispanics (full-time staff) and number employed
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the foundation currently employs persons of Hispanic origin full-time and the approximate number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsive foundations reported 12% having full-time Hispanic employees; use as internal diversity/capacity metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Hispanic consultants and number
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the foundation uses Hispanic consultants and, if so, how many.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record counts; reported 17% of responsive foundations used Hispanic consultants. Use as engagement/diversity indicator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification rules and assumptions for coding grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit coding assumptions used when classifying grants from the Foundation Grants Index (e.g., agencies with 'La Raza' in legal title considered Chicano; agencies with Puerto Rican history/culture in name considered Puerto Rican; such institutions assumed minority-controlled; bilingual/bicultural services in high-Hispanic areas assumed Hispanic beneficiary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and apply these rules consistently; recognize these assumptions may introduce bias—report limitations and perform spot checks and telephone follow-ups to verify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources and triangulation for researching foundation grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended data sources and methods: manual search of Foundation Grants Index (FGI), telephone and mail contact with foundations and grantees, analyses of annual reports, and mail surveys; avoid exclusive reliance on IRS Form 990-A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FGI is helpful but inaccurate in places; compensate via checking, spot checks, telephone verification, mail surveys and annual reports. Encourage multiple sources to increase validity and correct coding errors in the FGI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation Center coding accuracy and error correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Need to examine and improve the system used by the Foundation Center for coding and describing grants; researchers should report discovered errors and foundations should inform the Center of errors found in bi-monthly listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate collaborative correction processes between foundations, Foundation Center, and researchers; treat FGI data with caution until coding is improved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research credibility and collaboration recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations that NCRP advise researchers on study credibility, Council on Foundations engage in its own research and assist researchers in obtaining higher response rates, and the Foundation Center collaborate to improve data quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote coordinated efforts among major research/advocacy organizations to improve the state-of-the-art in foundation research; include best-practice methodological guidance in study designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural and outreach practices indicating an atypically responsive foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional policies and procedures associated with foundations responsive to Hispanics: having full-time staff, Hispanic board membership or employees, publishing annual/biennial reports, maintaining (general or Hispanic) mailing lists, answering inquiries, providing acknowledgements/rejection notices, offering feedback or technical assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these practices as a checklist for foundations aiming to increase access for Hispanic and other minority applicants. The monograph notes such practices are atypical among the overall foundation population but common among responsive foundations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional grouping for analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: States are grouped into regions for analysis of geographic distribution (e.g., Northeast: CT, MA, NY, NJ, PA, DC; North Central: IL, IN, MI, MN, OH, WI, NE; Southwest/West grouping including CA, AZ, TX, NM, CO; grants of national scope classified as 'national').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use predefined regional groupings consistently when computing regional distributions and when comparing to Hispanic population shares. Note that geographic coverage of grants cannot always be determined from FGI.
